objective: Test whether replacing one-source-per-cycle descriptor fill with direct ordered K4 extraction from already-sparse 16-bit masks materially accelerates the frozen M132 dualrow512 service recurrence.

finding.reason: The frozen recurrence serializes 119,447,791 PWP tokens and 124,730,596 correction tokens; faster descriptor production converts fill time into producer-bank stalls instead of shortening the critical service chain.
finding.decision: Do not implement a wide K4 descriptorizer as the next performance RTL milestone. Attack PWP/correction service overlap first.

architecture_assumption.input: already-sparse nonzero 16-bit source mask with row/block/sign metadata

paper_safe_statement: On the frozen heldout recurrence, reducing descriptor fill payload by 46.93% improves module cycles by only 0.322%; a second extractor lane adds only 0.014%. Descriptor production is therefore not the current critical performance target.
prohibited_claims: Do not call 1.436x versus compact256 a descriptorizer-only gain; most of that ratio is inherited from M132 dualrow512 PWP.
Do not claim RTL, physical, energy or system acceleration from this cycle DSE.
Do not assume the already-sparse mask source is free or implemented.
